# Selvi Turkish-field matcher package

Read `01-policy.md`, then `02-interface-guide.md`, with `openapi.json`. The English guide explains every request field and every response/product member. `expected.json` uses the check/expected/source format and asserts the complete api_fields object. Operation names and paths remain the seven English tool names. Calls and policy prose are English.

Differences from Brief A: three different identity questions (year, district text, six digits); two total wrong answers; two different bands with calendar-days and next-month day deadlines; percentage floors; Sunday–Thursday operations; no already-paid rule; dictated opening and consent wording; up to two products with notes; zero save retries; and different callback hours. No restructuring route exists either. No holidays apply; this intentionally uses other listed differences instead of introducing dated holiday assertions.

Matcher targets: every JSON payload property is Turkish, outside the stated English and six-language synonym sets. There is no description key anywhere. The only explicit English semantic mapping is in the separate bank guide. Multi-property requests/responses and product members are reordered; get_account's singleton request cannot meaningfully be reordered. Enums, types and date formats provide clues, but repeated strings and booleans cannot be disambiguated reliably by type alone: the extractor must retain the documented api_fields mappings. In particular, operation success, individual verification and whole-check verification are three different booleans. Customer and product identifiers are different strings. This is designed against the stated matcher coverage, not a claim about uninspected current matcher code.

Traps: note text comes first; close reason precedes outcome and customer; promise date precedes product, amount and customer; product fields start with lateness, then amount, then type, then identifier. Failed get_account may return an empty array with basarili=false; this is not evidence of no debt. No required-name-without-property trap is used.

The no-description constraint also removes the Response Object description required by formal OpenAPI 3.0 validation. This fixture deliberately satisfies the requested JSON/paths/body structure and no-description rule, not full OpenAPI meta-schema conformance. That unavoidable transport-metadata conflict is explicit rather than hidden.

Rounding: policy section 4 requires nearest-cent half-up. For a full balance of 10.02, the 25% floor is 2.51; a percent rule with banker's rounding is not equivalent. The percentage in expected.json is a structural assertion, not proof of the tie behavior. No pipeline was run to infer these values.

Validation: JSON parses, all seven operations are POST with JSON bodies, request/response/product properties match the documented Turkish vocabulary, required names exist, every expected API slot matches a schema property, and no description key exists. expected.json contains no concrete calendar dates: only relative deadline rules and an empty holiday list. Thus no expected date was calculated by hand and no prohibited import of bankcal.py was needed. No extraction, build, simulation or Freya call occurred. Scoring reference read first: https://www.freyavoice.ai/hackathon (ledger Outcome; transcript Policy/Honesty; all three repetitions must pass).
